input.command:
cat > diagnosis.json <<'EOF'
{"spec_element": "invariant",
 "proof_obligation": "bridge",
 "diagnosis": "The loop invariants of rolling_max only track |result| == i and m == result[i-1]; they say nothing about result[j] being the max of numbers[0..j+1] or m being the max of the prefix numbers[0..i]. So at loop exit (i == |numbers|) the invariants cannot imply the ensures clause forall i :: 0 < i < |result| ==> isMax(result[i], numbers[0..i+1]). Fix: strengthen invariants with isMax(m, numbers[0..i]) and forall j :: 0 <= j < i ==> isMax(result[j], numbers[0..j+1])."}
EOF
python3 - <<'EOF'
p='program.dfy'; s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace("""    invariant m == result[i-1]
""","""    invariant m == result[i-1]
    invariant isMax(m, numbers[0..i])
    invariant forall j :: 0 <= j < i ==> isMax(result[j], numbers[0..(j+1)])
""")
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
dafny verify program.dfy

content.text:
`program.dfy` now verifies: Dafny reports 4 verified, 0 errors.

**What was wrong:** the code in `rolling_max` was fine, but its loop invariants were too weak. They only said `|result| == i` and `m == result[i-1]`. Neither says anything about which values are the maximums. So when the loop ended, the invariants couldn't prove the postcondition `forall i :: 0 < i < |result| ==> isMax(result[i], numbers[0..(i+1)])`. In the task's terms this is an invariant/bridge failure, which is what I recorded in `diagnosis.json`.

**Fix:** I added two loop invariants and changed nothing else:
```dafny
invariant isMax(m, numbers[0..i])
invariant forall j :: 0 <= j < i ==> isMax(result[j], numbers[0..(j+1)])
```
The first says the running value `m` is the maximum of the first `i` numbers, which is what lets the second hold after each new element is appended. When the loop finishes, `i == |numbers|`, and the second invariant gives the postcondition directly.
